title: Tesserafin theme manifest (Theme Platform v2)
description: Universal theme manifest (RFC-0007 §4). One theme.json per theme directory under tesserafin-design/themes/<id>/. The manifest is a CLOSED declarative vocabulary: every object below sets additionalProperties:false and every leaf is an enum, a bounded pattern or a token value. That closure is the mechanism by which an imported theme cannot carry executable code, a network reference or a credential — there is no key it could arrive under. See RFC-0007 §6.

contractVersion.description: Theme Platform contract this manifest is written against. v1 (RFC-0005 §7.3) manifests omitted this key entirely; they are migrated, not silently accepted — see RFC-0007 §8.

id.description: namespace.name — e.g. "official.classic", "community.abyss-remix". STABLE IDENTITY: this value is the persisted user setting, the MUI color-scheme key and the generated stylesheet selector. Renaming a theme changes `name`, never `id`.

name.description: Human-readable display name, e.g. "Tesserafin Classic". This is the only user-facing name; `id` is not.

description.description: One-line description shown in pickers and in the Theme Studio.

compatibility.description: Per-platform Tesserafin version range this theme targets. At least one platform is required.

modes.description: Modes this theme provides color tokens for (tokens.json's `color` group).

profiles.description: Per-profile token overrides (RFC-0007 §4.3). Each value is a DEEP-PARTIAL of tokens.schema.json — the same closed vocabulary, with nothing required. v1 typed this as additionalProperties:true, which let an imported theme smuggle arbitrary keys through a profile; v2 closes it (RFC-0007 §6.2).

assets.description: Asset ROLES (RFC-0007 §4.5). A role maps to a package-relative path, never to a URL: the pattern forbids ':' and '//', so 'https://…', 'data:…' and 'javascript:…' are all unrepresentable. A renderer that has no asset for a role falls back to the built-in asset for that role.

presentation.description: Semantic component variants and declarative composition recipes (RFC-0007 §4.6/§4.7). These are SEMANTIC choices over published presentation primitives — never selectors, never DOM structure. A theme that omits a key gets the platform default for it.

text.description: Per-language wording for a closed set of semantic text slots (THEME-A2, docs/tesserafin/design-theme-text-slots.md). Plain text only; variables are named in braces and checked beyond this schema by the validator.

capabilities.description: Capabilities this theme uses (RFC-0007 §5.2). `required` means the theme is not renderable without them and a renderer lacking one must refuse to activate the theme and say why. `optional` means the theme degrades gracefully — the renderer falls back to the platform default for that capability.

renderers.description: Platform renderer layer (RFC-0007 §5). The universal layer above is platform-neutral; everything platform-specific is confined here, so adding a renderer never makes the universal contract Web-only.

lineage.description: Remix and source lineage (RFC-0007 §4.8). Recorded so a derived theme can always name what it derives from. This loop implements the metadata only — marketplace upload, signing, payment and source protection are out of scope (RFC-0007 §9).

remixable.description: Whether this theme's author permits derived themes. Declarative intent recorded in the manifest; it is not, and must not be presented as, a technical enforcement mechanism.

attribution.description: Attribution line a derived theme is asked to carry.

assetPath.description: Package-relative path. No scheme, no protocol, no parent traversal — a theme can only name a file it ships.

textSlots.description: The closed slot registry. A slot is listed only once a renderer surface reads it.

textLocale.description: A supported interface locale, normalised as globalize normalises it (lower case, `_` read as `-`).

capabilityName.description: A capability defined by RFC-0007 §5.2. The list is closed: an unknown capability name is a validation error, not an ignored extension, so a theme cannot claim a capability the platform has never defined.

titleLines.description: Lines a card title may take before it is cut. The theme's default: a call site that states its own keeps it, and an overlay title never takes fewer than two.

navigationVariant.description: Presentation of the primary navigation shell. It changes how navigation LOOKS, never what a user is allowed to reach: the set of destinations is authorization state, not theme state (RFC-0007 §6.1).

tabs.description: How in-page tabs (Home, a library's destinations) are drawn. Same tabs, same order, same keyboard contract.

sectionTitleVariant.description: One recipe for every section heading of Home, Library and Item Details, in every state. It changes how a heading looks, never its level, its text or whether it exists. `auto` keeps the page's own scale, including the Item Details hero's.

gridVariant.description: Media grid item size by semantic context. It scales the grid's minimum column width within bounds, never sets a length, never changes what is listed, and never overrides the user's own density choice.

pageRecipes.description: Declarative composition recipes. A recipe orders and selects PUBLISHED sections; it cannot introduce a section the renderer does not implement, because the section vocabulary is a closed enum.

backdrop.description: What stands behind the Home composition. `ambient` lays the hero's artwork, blurred and dimmed, behind the page; it re-uses the hero's image and issues no request of its own.

itemDetails.description: The Item Details recipe. `hero` selects an artwork LAYOUT treatment — it never causes an extra request, never overrides the user's details-banner setting, never gives a Person or a Book a backdrop, and the poster is rendered under all three. `sections` orders and selects durable user-facing CONTENT FAMILIES. The enum widened from five to eleven names in #129 Step 2, when the route began reading the recipe: the original five are retained verbatim so every manifest valid before remains valid, and the six additions are the families the five could not name. None of these is a DOM identifier, a component name or an item type, and there is deliberately no name for the item's identity, its action bar, its track selectors, its user-data controls, its recording editor, a permission gate or a warning — those are fixed regions outside theme authority (RFC-0007 §6.1).

hero.description: The artwork layout. `immersive` makes the item's backdrop a full-width lead band with the identity, facts and actions over its foot and the poster as an inset; it reads the backdrop `backdrop` reads, so it adds no request, and it falls back to the `poster` layout wherever the band cannot render (no backdrop, a Person or a Book, or the user's details banner turned off).

controls.description: How the fixed action bar and track selectors are dressed. `form`: rectangular buttons and labelled selector rows. `pill`: a large play pill, outlined secondary pills, round icon actions and one row of selector chips with the label inside. The same controls, order, labels, states and keyboard behaviour exist under both.

people.description: How cast and crew are drawn: `cards` (poster cards, name and role below) or `portraits` (round head-shots, name centred below). Same people, order and links.

facts.description: How the item's people, studio and genre lists are grouped. `table` gives each list a labelled row; `inline` runs the values together on one line under the title, keeping the labels for assistive technology. Neither changes which lists exist, their order, their links or their data.

backdrop.description: What stands behind the Item Details composition. `ambient` lays the poster the page already shows, blurred and dimmed, behind the page; it issues no request of its own and shows nothing for an item without a poster.

webRenderer.description: Web renderer declaration. `supports` is the renderer's own capability list, read by the resolver to decide fallback. `source` is the RESERVED extension point for the advanced CSS/SCSS/LESS/Sass authoring layer (RFC-0007 §7): its shape is fixed here so the package format does not have to change when a compiler boundary is proven, but the only value this contract accepts today is kind "none". Nothing in the universal layer above depends on this object, which is what keeps the contract from becoming Web-only.

kind.description: RESERVED. "scss"/"less"/"sass" are deliberately NOT accepted yet: accepting them before an isolated compiler boundary exists would publish a promise the renderer cannot keep. Widening this enum is the single schema change that opens §7.

reservedRenderer.description: RESERVED for a future native renderer (Android/TV, Apple). Only `supports` is meaningful today; a renderer that does not exist declares nothing.

tokensPartial.description: Deep-partial of tokens.schema.json: same groups, same leaf constraints, nothing required. Kept structurally in step with tokens.schema.json by tesserafin-design/__tests__/schema-partial-parity.test.ts, which fails if a token group is added there and not here.

cssLength.description: A CSS length with a unit, or the bare unitless zero ("0") that stylelint's length-zero-no-unit rule requires.
